Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

LENS: swapping and page replacement. Scrutinise alloc_user_page, selete_page, write_to_sd and the swap-in path of alloc_page_helper in kernel/mm/mm.c. Check: disk slot leaks/double allocation, the PTE encoding used for a swapped-out page (_PAGE_SOFT + pfn=slot) versus a never-mapped PTE of 0, the user_page[].pgtable back-pointer becoming stale, evicting a page that is pinned or shared, sbi_sd_read/sbi_sd_write block arithmetic against SWAP_BEGIN/DISK_PAGE_NUM and the image layout, memset of a page that is about to be overwritten by a disk read, infinite loops or assert(0) reachable in normal operation.

  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SSTATUS(sp)
  csrw CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SEPC(sp)
  csrw CSR_SEPC, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_STVAL(sp)
  csrw CSR_STVAL, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SCAUSE(sp)
  csrw CSR_SCAUSE, t0
  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SSCRATCH(sp)
  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, t0

  addi sp, sp, (OFFSET_SIZE)
  sd sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
.endm

/* 
 * trick: during an irq handling, current_running may be modified
 * but $tp will not be modified until ret_from_exception()
 */
ENTRY(enable_preempt)
  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  beq t0, zero, do_enable
  addi t0, t0, -1
  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  beq t0, zero, do_enable
  jr ra
do_enable:
  not t0, x0
  csrs CSR_SIE, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_preempt)

ENTRY(disable_preempt)
  csrw CSR_SIE, zero  
  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  addi t0, t0, 1
  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_preempt)

ENTRY(enable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_interrupt)

ENTRY(disable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_interrupt)

ENTRY(enable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_sum)

ENTRY(disable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_sum)

ENTRY(ret_from_exception)
  ld tp, current_cpu_running
  call unlock_kernel
  RESTORE_CONTEXT

  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, to_user
to_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
  j restore_sp_done
to_user:
  ld sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
restore_sp_done:
  sret
ENDPROC(ret_from_exception)

ENTRY(exception_handler_entry)
  /* use kernel stack to handle exception */
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, from_user

from_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  j store_sp_done
from_user:
  sd sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
store_sp_done:

  SAVE_CONTEXT
  /* 
   * Disable user-mode memory access as it should only be set in the actual user copy routines.
   * Disable the FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space.
   */
  li t0, SR_SUM | SR_FS
  csrc sstatus, t0

  /* load the global pointer */
  .option push
  .option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
  .option pop

  call lock_kernel
  /* 
   * load ret_from_exception into $ra
   * so that we can return to ret_from_exception
   * when interrupt_helper complete.
   */
  la ra, ret_from_exception
  
  /* call interrupt_helper and pass parameters for it */
  mv a0, sp
  csrr a1, CSR_STVAL
  csrr a2, CSR_SCAUSE
  j interrupt_helper
ENDPROC(exception_handler_entry)

ENTRY(clear_ipi)
  li t0, SIE_SSIE
  csrc CSR_SIP, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(clear_ipi)

findings.title: write_to_sd copies the victim frame to disk before invalidating its PTE, so concurrent user writes on the other hart are silently lost
findings.detail: write_to_sd() (mm.c:123-149) does `sbi_sd_write(pa, ...)` first (line 134) and only afterwards clears _PAGE_PRESENT / sets _PAGE_SOFT / calls flush_tlb_all() (lines 140-147). The kernel lock (kernel/sched/smp.c:30) is released by ret_from_exception before `sret` (arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S:157), so while hart 0 is inside write_to_sd, hart 1 can be executing user code in the very address space that owns the victim frame. Concrete failure: process P runs on hart 1 with va V -> frame F mapped writable (alloc_page_helper always grants _PAGE_WRITE|_PAGE_DIRTY, mm.c:233). Hart 0 takes a page fault for another task, alloc_user_page (mm.c:60-65) finds no free frame, selete_page() returns F, write_to_sd snapshots F to swap slot i. Hart 1 then stores 0xdead to V — the PTE is still present and its TLB entry is still valid, so the store lands in F. Hart 0 now clears _PAGE_PRESENT, flushes, frees F, memsets it (mm.c:75) and hands it to the new owner. When P later faults on V, alloc_page_helper reads back the pre-store copy from slot i: P's write has vanished with no error. The invalidate+shootdown must happen before the sbi_sd_write, not after. The same window also lets a stale remote TLB entry write into a frame hart 0 has already memset and reassigned to a different process.

findings.title: Eviction can steal the caller's own user pages mid-syscall; the resulting S-mode page fault deadlocks on the non-recursive kernel lock
findings.detail: do_exec() (sched.c:185-256) calls enable_sum() at line 189 and keeps user pointers `file_name` and `argv[]` (which point into the *caller's* address space) live across init_page_table() (line 219, ~6 frames), alloc_user_page() for the kernel stack (line 221) and load_elf() (line 244, more frames). Every one of those may run alloc_user_page -> selete_page(), and selete_page (mm.c:104-116) skips only `pin` and `pgtable == NULL` frames — the shell's own stack page holding argv[i] and the argv strings is an ordinary unpinned frame and is a legal victim. init_user_stack() then dereferences it at sched.c:156-158 (`strlen(argv[i])`, `memcpy(..., argv[i], len)`). Because the page is now _PAGE_SOFT, that load traps in S-mode; exception_handler_entry unconditionally executes `call lock_kernel` (arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S:199) and lock_kernel is a plain non-recursive spin_lock_acquire (kernel/sched/smp.c:30, kernel/locking/lock.c:9-17) that this hart already holds — both harts wedge forever, with no console output. Nothing pins the caller's argv/file_name pages (or copies them into kernel memory) for the duration of the call, and handle_page_fault has no way to report failure. The same hazard applies to do_process_show/do_show_exec, which write into a user buffer under SUM.

findings.title: selete_page clears _PAGE_ACCESSED without a TLB shootdown, so the reference bit is never re-set and NRU degenerates
findings.detail: selete_page (mm.c:111-114) does `clear_attribute(user_page[i].pgtable, _PAGE_ACCESSED)` and continues, with no local_flush_tlb_page/flush_tlb_all anywhere in the sweep (the only flush is inside write_to_sd, mm.c:147, after a victim is already chosen). On RISC-V the A bit is written by the page-table walker; a hit in the TLB performs no walk, so once the in-memory bit has been cleared it stays clear for every page whose translation is still cached. Concrete failure: under memory pressure the first clock sweep clears A on all resident frames; on the second sweep every frame looks unreferenced, so the very first candidate is evicted regardless of how hot it is — including the page holding the instruction that just faulted or the current user stack page, which immediately refaults and forces another eviction. The intended second-chance behaviour never happens and the policy degrades to plain FIFO with extra 4 KB disk writes.

findings.title: alloc_user_page zeroes the whole 4 KB frame that the swap-in path immediately overwrites with sbi_sd_read
findings.detail: alloc_user_page unconditionally does `memset((void*)pa2kva(pa), 0, PAGE_SIZE)` (mm.c:75) before returning. In the swap-in branch of alloc_page_helper (mm.c:222-223) the very next statement is `sbi_sd_read((unsigned int)pa, PAGE_SD_BLOCKS, ...)`, which overwrites all 4096 bytes. Every page brought back from swap therefore pays a full-page zeroing that is discarded — and the zeroing happens on the critical path of a page fault, with the global kernel lock held and both harts serialised behind it. The memset is only needed on the fresh-allocation path (mm.c:229) where it prevents leaking the previous owner's data; the swap-in path should skip it (e.g. by an extra argument or by allocating raw and zeroing at the call site).

findings.title: Swap area holds only 256 slots for 53248 frames and exhausting it panics the kernel instead of failing the allocation
findings.detail: write_to_sd allocates a slot with a linear scan and `assert(i != DISK_PAGE_NUM)` (mm.c:126-131); DISK_PAGE_NUM is 256 while USER_PAGE_NUM is (0x5e000000-0x51000000)/4096 = 53248. Every eviction consumes a slot unconditionally — there is no _PAGE_DIRTY check, so clean, never-written pages (the read-only ELF text pages that init_page_table maps at mm.c:259-261, which could simply be dropped and reloaded) burn slots too. Once physical memory fills, the 257th eviction hits assert(0) and takes down the whole kernel rather than failing the one allocation; alloc_user_page (mm.c:50) has no failure return and handle_page_fault (mm.c:406) ignores the result, so there is no path to kill just the offending process. do_exec's guard `free_page_num() < EXEC_MIN_FREE_PAGES` (sched.c:212) counts physical frames only and never looks at disk_page[], so it cannot prevent this. selete_page's own `assert(0)` (mm.c:119) is the same class of unrecoverable exit.
